adjudicator: Human review supplied in this task
criterion: Whether the request merits an additional Planner call before entering Agent Runtime, under the Stage 1.5 Router ADR.

cases.rationale: A bounded seven-day count and per-person total are structured aggregation that Runtime can perform directly; there is no dependency between investigation stages.
The request depends on an ordered evidence chain: find A/B differences, trace adoption versus shelving, then identify evidence that led to the final choice.
Summarizing TypeScript views from the last seven days is bounded retrieval and synthesis; the word “summarize” alone is not a planning signal.

A six-month trend summary does not request turning points, a causal chain, or an investigation whose next stage depends on an earlier result. Time span and trend wording alone do not justify Planner. Explicitly tracing a shift, finding its key time, and explaining which feedback caused it would be planned.
Explaining the change from an initial recommendation to later rejection and what happened in between requires longitudinal state and causal investigation.
The request must connect opposing evidence, explain why the alternative was retained, and resolve contradictions by checking chronology; later reasoning depends on earlier evidence.
Prior context asks for the full decision evolution and test evidence. The short follow-up inherits that multi-stage investigation.
Prior context limits the request to summarizing one already-provided reason and explicitly says not to investigate other discussions. Planner adds no useful stage.
The request explicitly calls for recovery: if a source is not found, reformulate the search from new clues and continue until the evidence source is found.
A people count and weekly breakdown are structured aggregation; returning two fields does not make this a multi-stage investigation.
Identifying which discussions drove the A-to-B change and explaining why requires linking evidence across time.
The request returns to unresolved prior work, asks for missing context, and then asks to reassess the basis; this is explicit recovery.
Explaining one term in one message is a single semantic lookup. The word “analyze” does not itself trigger Planner.
Reconstructing the sequence from initial recommendation through counterexample to revised advice is a longitudinal state transition.
Returning one sentence for each of three tools is bounded retrieval and synthesis; item count alone is not planning complexity.
Comparing views and supporters of two options does not ask for evolution, causality, or cross-stage validation; ordinary aggregation is sufficient.
